vram_note: box card is the 72 GB variant; campaign budgets are computed against the 48 GB production cap (49152 MB) - campaign policy, not a measurement

datasheet.notes: product page headline is 2064 AI TOPS = FP4 sparse; dense ladder FP4/2 = FP8, FP8/2 = FP16, INT8 TOPS = FP8 TFLOPS per NVIDIA RTX Blackwell PRO GPU Architecture v1.0 Table 4; fp32 = 14080 cores x 2 x 2.377 GHz official boost = 66.9 TFLOPS (re-derived 2026-08-14 from SP-12389-001_v06 Table 2-1, which revised the boost clock 2026-08-13 — the earlier 73.7 assumed 2.617 GHz; measured 42.5 is now ~64% attainment). Clock ladder per the same table: base 1755 / boost 2377 / max-boost 3090 (max-boost is what clocks.max.graphics reports — a best-case bin, not a sustained promise). Power capping: 300 W threshold, 50 ms typical / 100 ms max response; EDPp allows ~540 W over 400 us windows (SP-12389-001_v06 Tables 2-9/2-10) — the electrical basis of burst-vs-governed. Bandwidth 1,344 GB/s stated as 'up to', max memory clock 14 GHz (both 48/72 GB variants). Clock basis (2026-08-18, benchmark-guide thread): DA-12900-001 Introduction attributes 2,377 MHz to RTX PRO 5000 and 2,617 MHz to RTX PRO 6000 WSE (confirmed by NVIDIA), BUT the guide's Table 4 peak column for the 5000 itself computes at ~2.6 GHz (fp16 293 = 110 SMs x 0.25 inst/clk x 4096 x ~2.6 GHz; fp32 74 = 14080x2x2.63), and their measured fp16 288 implies ~2.56 GHz realized — above the stated 2,377 max (light-load boost; 3,090 max-boost bin exists). Refined: EVERY SKU's peak column in the guide's Tables 4-5 implies a clock ~8-10% above that SKU's stated max (5000 ~2.61 vs 2.377; 6000 Max-Q ~2.37 vs 2.200; 6000 WSE ~2.83 vs 2.617) — a systematic basis question, not a SKU mixup; still open with NVIDIA. Campaign numbers unaffected: our judgments use 2,377-based derivations (fp32 66.9) and measured-vs-measured agreements at matched locked clocks.

open_items: ECC is configurable and DISABLED by default (SP-12389-001_v06 Table 2-3); ceilings + byte budgets were measured in the default state. If the product ships ECC-on, re-measure the bandwidth ceiling and re-run the dial before final sizing - bandwidth is the decisive axis

Programmable power (-pl, down to ~150 W; persistent via SMBPBI) enables a power-matched per-watt experiment vs Thor (e.g. -pl 150) - optional, would replace the nameplate-based 2-2.6x per-watt estimate with a measured one
MIG with two instances is supported (Table 2-1) - a hardware-isolation option for the composition/fleet phase (pin a latency-critical model per instance)

clock_sources.note: prefer a persistent pynvml handle; nvidia-smi subprocess fallback allowed at reduced rate

sm_lock_note: sustained-bin SM lock (2026-08-12) + power-governed adjudication (same day): the 2160 request realizes 2092 cold and settles 2047-2062 warm at the 300 W cap (3-min soak wanders to 1897 while throughput holds within 10%). No useful SM clock is truly pinnable on this part - the governor holds POWER, not clock - so the lock stayed at 2160 as an upper bound and drift_report.py's power-governed rule (mem PASS + sw_power_cap only + sm median dev <= 10%) demotes the floating SM clock to recorded-data with a WARN verdict. A dev beyond 10% or any hw/thermal reason still FAILs. AMENDED 2026-08-19: lowered to 2062, the warm-settled bin. The tool_tracking run exposed a hole in the 2160-upper-bound policy: a light workload (~176 W, 1.2 ms kernels) floats 2062-2152 with NO sw_power_cap flag asserted, so the power-governed demotion cannot apply and drift hard-FAILs (pct_at_target 14.8%). Locking the holdable bin keeps requested==realized for every workload class - the same honest-terms logic as mem_lock_note. Evidence: results_rtx_tool_tracking/models/tool_tracking/clock_samples.csv (median 2062, zero throttle reasons, 176 W) vs its provenance/lock_verified.json (2137 flat under GEMM load). Ceilings remain certified at the 2026-08-12 policy (realized-2092 reference)
mem_lock_note: nameplate 14001 MHz does not hold under tensor load on this card - memory pins one supported bin down at 13365; locking there keeps requested==realized so verify_lock judges on honest terms (measured 2026-08-07)

power_sources.note: power.draw via NVML/nvidia-smi - no sysfs rails on discrete

emc_dial.note: memory/SM sensitivity via -lmc/-lgc at 80% of max inside the pipeline (RUN_CLOCK_DIAL=1); no devfreq dial on discrete

ops_per_tinst_note: fp16 calibrated on-box 2026-08-12 (calibrate_ops_per_tinst.py, known-truth 137.44 GFLOP GEMM: 2^25 tensor insts, snap error 0.00%) - note 4x sm_110's 1024, constants do NOT transfer across architectures. int8/fp8 remain uncalibrated: when the first int8/fp8 model campaign runs here, calibrate against a known-truth engine at that precision first or the roofline will refuse those pipes
quirks: -lgc/-lmc can silently not take (observed 2026-07: locked file read 180/405 MHz while log claimed 3090/14001) - verify under load, never trust an idle read-back

SM lock realizes at the boost-table tensor-load clock (~2570 observed for a 3090 request), and the realized clock is WORKLOAD-DEPENDENT at the power cap (2437 under a light GEMM, 2167 under a heavy one) - hence the sm_lock_mhz sustained-bin policy; the reference clock is the REALIZED value, never the requested one

torch typed int8 path (_int_mm) failed on sm_120 with pre-cu13x builds (cuBLAS INVALID_VALUE) - run the GEMM canary before trusting torch probes; int8 ceiling falls back to the TRT path if typed probes fail
idle discrete GPUs legitimately downclock even when locked - an idle clock read proves nothing about the lock
sampler_period_note: 73.1 ms: not commensurate with 20/30 Hz row periods. NVML power.draw is a ~1 s hardware average on this card (aliasing does not bite as it did with Thor's instantaneous ina238 register), the period is kept for consistency with the Thor sweep
_README: A filled, working example (RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell, discrete). Values from the public product page plus this card's own lock/drift measurements. Copy the template for other devices. Machine-specific configs you add should be named <name>.local.json (gitignored).
required_power_mode_note: jetson-only (nvpmodel); null on discrete, where the power cap is a -pl setting rather than a mode
